title: A Wobbling, Peanut-Shaped Asteroid Reshaped by Sunlight
hook: NASA's Lucy found that asteroid Donaldjohanson is a peanut-shaped relic of an ancient collision — slowly reshaped by sunlight, and still carrying traces of old water.
key_points: NASA's Lucy spacecraft studied the asteroid Donaldjohanson up close.
It is peanut-shaped and wobbling, born from a violent ancient collision.
Sunlight has slowly reshaped it — light carries momentum and can nudge small bodies.
It also carries traces of ancient water, a clue to the early solar system.
content_html: According to a ScienceDaily report, NASA's Lucy spacecraft flew past the asteroid Donaldjohanson and found a wobbling, peanut-shaped world. Its lumpy form is thought to be the leftover of a violent ancient collision, and it has been slowly reshaped since then by an unlikely sculptor: sunlight. Light carries momentum, so over very long times the gentle, uneven push of sunlight on an irregular body can subtly change how it spins and how it is shaped.
extra_html: The asteroid also carries traces of ancient water, which makes it a useful clue to the solar system's distant past — a record of where water and raw materials sat among the small bodies that formed billions of years ago. Missions like Lucy visit these leftovers precisely because they are time capsules: little changed since the era of planet formation, they preserve evidence that has long since been erased on larger, more active worlds.
